nodes.rationale: The audited real web app's design tokens (oklch electric-lavender, Outfit+Inter fonts, full dark mode) supersede the earlier PDF blueprint's guessed tokens, since the real screenshots are treated as ground truth.

nodes.label: delete_current_user SECURITY DEFINER RPC
nodes.rationale: Performs a hard delete (bypassing soft-delete) across ph_readings, daily_logs, cycle_settings, profiles and auth.users, intentionally for GDPR/Play erasure compliance rather than the app's usual soft-delete pattern.

nodes.label: Google Sign-In (Credential Manager)
nodes.rationale: Native Google Credential Manager flow chosen over the Lovable web OAuth wrapper; fails safely rather than faking success on cancellation, network loss, or an unconfigured/unregistered signing certificate, since only the certificate registered in Google Cloud can complete the token exchange.

nodes.label: Hydration Tracking (waterMl canonical unit)
nodes.rationale: waterMl stays the canonical storage/sync/goal unit while ml/cups is purely a display preference, so switching display units can never change stored values, streak scoring, or synced data.

nodes.label: join_waitlist SECURITY DEFINER RPC
nodes.rationale: Direct table upsert required SELECT privilege that was deliberately withheld so the email list could never be enumerated with the anon key, causing every 1.3.1 join to fail with 401; the RPC does an untargeted on-conflict-do-nothing insert so silent duplicate no-op and an unreadable list can both be satisfied at once.

nodes.label: Learn Article Date-Based Drip
nodes.rationale: Switched from weeks-since-first-open to fixed calendar dates (Article.publishedAt) as the agreed cross-platform contract with iOS, so every reader sees a given article on the same real day regardless of when they first opened the app.

nodes.label: Local-Only Meal Logging (Room v8)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately kept local-only (no Supabase table, no sync) as an owner-approved scope decision so the iOS build sharing the same backend project is left untouched by the new feature.

nodes.label: Offline-First Sync Queue (daily logs, pH, supplements)
nodes.rationale: Offline writes land as PENDING_UPSERT and are drained by WorkManager instead of being refused, because refusing a save served no purpose once refresh() was made to skip rows with unsynced local changes — the rule that makes offline writes safe.
nodes.norm_label: offline-first sync queue (daily logs, ph, supplements)

nodes.label: Vaginal pH Tracking Feature
nodes.rationale: Migrated from urine pH to vaginal pH with a two-band model (Healthy 3.8–4.5 / Elevated >4.5) after client approval; syncs to Supabase via PhRepository with a WorkManager retry queue, disclosed explicitly in the card copy rather than presented as local-only.

nodes.label: Production ph_value_range CHECK constraint
nodes.rationale: The urine-era CHECK (4.5–9.0) survived the vaginal-pH migration and silently rejected every reading in the lower Healthy band (3.8–4.5), so it was replaced with a measurement-type-aware constraint (vaginal 3.8–7.0, urine legacy 4.5–9.0) in a single pre-checked transaction.

nodes.label: Room Local Database (schema v2→v8)
nodes.rationale: Destructive fallback migration removed in favor of explicit MIGRATION_x_y steps so upgrades preserve local data (especially local-only pH readings) instead of wiping the database.

nodes.label: Seven Bottom Navigation Tabs (incl. dedicated pH tab)
nodes.rationale: pH was promoted to its own bottom tab reusing the canonical tracker/ph route (client-chosen layout, add rather than displace) so Home, Track, Insights and the deep link all resolve to one surface instead of a duplicate.
nodes.norm_label: seven bottom navigation tabs (incl. dedicated ph tab)

nodes.label: StreakEngine (4-of-7 weekly streak contract)
nodes.rationale: Weeks count as complete at 4 of 7 logged days (WEEK_COMPLETE_DAYS=4); when the tracking-vector spec and the engine disagree, the spec is treated as authoritative and the engine is changed to match it.

nodes.label: Supabase Backend (Auth + PostgREST + RPCs)
nodes.rationale: Native app calls Supabase directly (RLS enforces per-user isolation) instead of routing through the web app's server functions, since native clients cannot hold a service-role key.

nodes.label: Per-Supplement Daily Reminders
nodes.rationale: Reminder times are stored only in DataStore (never in the shared schema) and cleared on sign-out/deletion, and the lock-screen notification is name-free by design so the reminder itself can't disclose what a woman takes on a shared device.

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Tracking Test Vectors (tracking_test_vectors.json)
nodes.rationale: Mirrored verbatim into the iOS repo so a single spec file, not each platform's own engine, is authoritative for streak/hydration metrics; a metric that drifts on either platform fails the build.

nodes.label: Manual Supplement Entry + Genesyx Range (Room v6)
nodes.rationale: Shipped in source only and gated from release because the user_supplements/genesyx_products Supabase migration was REST-probed as not yet applied (PGRST205); shipping without it would break for signed-in users.
nodes.norm_label: manual supplement entry + genesyx range (room v6)

nodes.label: ArticleBookmarkEntity (Room)
nodes.rationale: Bookmarks placed in Room, not DataStore, because AuthRepository.clearAllTables() already wipes Room on account deletion — giving GDPR-safe deletion with zero new deletion code, whereas a DataStore stringSet would silently survive account deletion.

nodes.label: Six-Tab Bottom Nav Decision
nodes.rationale: Revised twice during implementation: first argued Learn should stay off the bar since Material 3 caps NavigationBar at 3-5 items; then proposed swapping Learn in for Profile since Profile is reachable from the Home avatar menu; the owner wanted Profile visible in the bar regardless, so the final shape carries six tabs, one past the Material 3 maximum — a deliberate product call, forcing labels to 9sp with no headroom for a seventh tab.

nodes.label: Article Content Model
nodes.rationale: Body modeled as sealed interface ArticleBlock instead of adding a Markdown dependency for ~14 bundled articles — smaller, type-safe, previewable, and serializable if content ever moves server-side. relatedArticleIds used instead of embedded Article references because a self-referencing data class graph can't be built as a val list without lateinit/lazy workarounds.

nodes.label: Learn Section Feature
nodes.rationale: Content bundled in-app rather than a Supabase articles table: matches the existing in-code content pattern, content changes at app-release cadence not CMS cadence, keeps the local-first architecture (Room = user data only), works offline with no loading state, and avoids a Play Data Safety question — with the direct cautionary precedent of PhRepository querying a not-yet-deployed table and logging errors after every sign-in.

nodes.label: pH Wellness Article Cluster
nodes.rationale: Gated on named clinical review before shipping; the other ten launch articles do not depend on it. Precedent: an earlier onboarding quiz modal claiming pH could influence fetal sex was caught as a launch blocker and removed — the cluster's absolute prohibitions (no conception/fetal-sex claims, no 'optimize/balance/correct' framing, no douching/alkaline-diet endorsement, no normal/abnormal labeling) exist to prevent that mistake recurring in softer language.

nodes.label: Phase D: pH Latest-Reading Fix
nodes.rationale: PhTrackerCard alone picked its 'latest' reading positionally (readings.lastOrNull()) instead of by timestamp like Track and Home (maxByOrNull{recordedAt}); it relied on the DAO's lexicographic ORDER BY over a TEXT column, and a server round-trip could drop the UTC offset and reorder rows, making the card disagree with other screens.

nodes.label: Phase A: Cycle Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Diagnosis found exactly one phase algorithm (CycleEngine.getCyclePhase) with no duplicates; both bugs were divergent inputs from un-keyed remember state freezing stale snapshots (dialog, HomeScreen cycleSeed, Track/CycleDetailScreen's frozen 'today'). Fixed by keying state to the latest repository emission rather than extracting a redundant CycleCalculator, since one already existed and every screen already called it.
nodes.norm_label: phase a: cycle single source of truth

nodes.label: SeedTestData Manual Seeder
nodes.rationale: Guarded by a @SeedOnly annotation plus a gradle notAnnotation instrumentation runner argument so CI/gradle never executes it; run only by hand via am instrument.

nodes.label: Phase B: Hydration Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Only one persisted hydration value exists (daily_logs.waterMl), so no new HydrationRepository was needed; the four disagreeing on-screen numbers came from three write/read defects (Log Today clobbering quick-adds via a stale snapshot, Nutrition reading a stale side-channel value, and unsynchronized read-modify-write races on quick-add) — fixed with a mutex-serialized mutateRow rather than a new store.
nodes.norm_label: phase b: hydration single source of truth

nodes.label: Phase C: Sleep Editor Fix
nodes.rationale: The editor collapsed 'no entry' to 0 minutes with no loaded gate before Room's first emission, so the stepper displayed a phantom zero and the user rebuilt their night on top of it; fixed by making todayMinutes nullable and gating the editor's composition on a loaded flag.

nodes.label: Google Sign-in Debug-Build Triage
nodes.rationale: Google sign-in fails on debug builds because only the release signing certificate is registered as an Android OAuth client in Google Cloud, not the debug SHA-1 — an environment/config gap, not an app-code regression, since the day's changes never touched auth.

nodes.label: Phase E: Pace Tiers, Honest Average, One Formatter, Banner Re-verify
nodes.rationale: Switched the 7-day hydration average from calendar-day division to logged-days division so both comparison windows count consistently and the stat isn't diluted by unlogged days — the old calendar division produced a near-meaningless average; also added a WELL_BEHIND coaching tier plus a dedicated zero-log line, since the existing two-tier maths produced an odd 'a little behind' message at 0ml logged.
nodes.norm_label: phase e: pace tiers, honest average, one formatter, banner re-verify

nodes.label: Phase F: P2 Polish (pH Chart, Slider, Legacy Labels)
nodes.norm_label: phase f: p2 polish (ph chart, slider, legacy labels)

nodes.label: Phase 2: Supplement Card + Hydration-Goal Bug Fix
nodes.rationale: Found during fact-checking that HydrationInsightLogic held a private hardcoded GOAL_ML=2400 that shadowed the user's actually-set hydration goal, so a user on a 3000ml goal had Insights bars scored against 2400; invisible because the two values happened to be equal by default. Fixed by threading the real goal from PreferencesRepository through compute().
nodes.norm_label: phase 2: supplement card + hydration-goal bug fix

nodes.label: Phase 0: Supplement Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: The wire format (supplement string names) was kept unchanged because daily_logs.supplements is a shared text[] column that iOS reads and writes; renaming those strings would have scored every Android-logged day as zero on iPhone and required a production backfill, so Supplement.wireName maps ids to the existing legacy strings instead.

nodes.label: Phase 1: WeekBuckets Unification
nodes.rationale: Consolidated two duplicated week-bucketing implementations into one ISO Monday-start definition; correctness of the refactor was proven by StreakEngineTest, TrackingVectorTest, and HydrationInsightLogicTest all passing unmodified, which mattered because the tracking vectors are mirrored verbatim into the iOS repo.

nodes.label: Default-ON Reminder Toggle Defect
nodes.rationale: pushEnabled defaults to true in DataStore, but work is only ever enqueued inside ProfileViewModel.setPush(), which runs only when the user touches the switch — so on a fresh install the switch reads ON while no permission was ever granted and no work was ever scheduled, directly contradicting the code's own doc comment that the switch can never sit on while notifications are silently dropped.

nodes.label: Notifications Audit (Part A)
nodes.rationale: Scoped explicitly to the parked, unshipped, flag-gated feature/partner-invites branch, since on main and on PR #9 zero notification files exist and PUSH_NOTIFICATIONS is false — nothing in the audited code reaches a user today.

nodes.label: v1.1 Notifications & Learn Brief
nodes.rationale: Explicitly grounded in the code as it exists today rather than CLAUDE.md, because CLAUDE.md was found stale in three load-bearing ways: versionCode, pH-sync status, and a KDoc claiming pH sync guards exist when they don't.

nodes.label: Reminder/Learn Deep Linking
nodes.rationale: MainActivity has no launchMode today (defaults to standard); tapping a notification while foregrounded would create a second MainActivity instance with a duplicate nav graph and a zombie back stack, so android:launchMode="singleTop" plus an onNewIntent override that calls handleDeepLink is required, which in turn requires hoisting navController out of setContent to an activity-level field.

nodes.label: Notification Channels
nodes.rationale: Four flat channels chosen deliberately over one-per-reminder-type: users manage channels in system settings and six switches is a wall.

nodes.label: POST_NOTIFICATIONS Permission State Machine
nodes.rationale: Never call the permission launcher cold: on Android 13+ the system dialog only shows twice, after which it silently no-ops with no distinguishing callback, so the app must show its own pre-permission sheet first and persist lastPromptedAt to disambiguate NOT_ASKED from DENIED_PERMANENT. The sheet is shown only at the moment the user flips their first reminder toggle (not during onboarding) because that is the one moment the ask is self-evidently justified.

nodes.label: NotificationSettings Model
nodes.rationale: Deliberately omits notificationChannelPreference (OS owns sound/vibration/importance on API 26+, an in-app mirror can only disagree with reality) and deepLinkTarget (that belongs on ReminderKind, compile-checked, not on mutable settings).

nodes.label: ReminderNotifier / shouldPost
nodes.rationale: All suppression enforcement centralized in one pure, unit-tested function (shouldPost) rather than scattered across workers, so quiet hours, caps, and gating rules are testable and consistent.

nodes.label: ReminderScheduler
nodes.rationale: Uses OneTimeWorkRequest with a computed initialDelay and self-rescheduling chain, not PeriodicWorkRequest, because PeriodicWorkRequest has a 15-minute minimum interval and no guarantee of when inside the period it fires — unacceptable for a reminder whose value is being at an exact time. Uses ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE (vs PhSyncScheduler's KEEP) because a settings change makes the old schedule wrong and it should be discarded, not deduplicated against.

nodes.label: Reminders Feature
nodes.rationale: Local WorkManager scheduling chosen over FCM/push because every reminder is a function of local state and the clock; avoids a new Data Safety disclosure, device-token lifecycle, and a Firebase project, and stays strictly additive if server-initiated campaigns are needed later.
